theater: 達達尼爾海峽與希俄斯灣

battle.name: 英土戰爭 (1807年-1812年)
battle.theater: 達達尼爾海峽與希俄斯灣
battle.brief: 英土戰爭自1807年英軍戰列艦隊強行通過達達尼爾海峽打開缺口開始。英軍在希俄斯灣擊毀奧斯曼分艦隊，隨後封鎖海峽，控制通往印度的航路。卡面這件長槍源於十六世紀西班牙大方陣，到1807年只剩兩個棲身處：英國水兵的登船矛，與奧軍中央的長矛線。

kit.name: 長槍
kit.history: 方陣的長矛讓火槍隊站在後面。密西西比之後，長矛和火槍一起站住了。

countries: 交戰一方是1807年的大英帝國海軍。指揮系統分兩層：倫敦的海軍部決定政策與艦隊調度，地中海方面的最高指揮交由海軍上將，實際在海峽開火的是約翰·托馬斯·達克沃思爵士率領的分艦隊，骨幹是七十四門砲戰列艦，配巡防艦與皇家海軍陸戰隊的登船突擊隊。英方的目標是取得達達尼爾海峽的通航權，同時削弱法國在東地中海的盟友——自1806年法奧同盟成立，這一戰略需要就變得急迫。交戰另一方是奧斯曼帝國：海軍歸凱普丹·帕夏統率，母港在君士坦丁堡與愛琴海群島之間；陸軍以大維齊爾與軍隊總督節制，兵源包括奧克式常備步兵、安納托利亞與魯梅利亞的省軍、西帕希騎兵，以及從克里米亞、高加索與巴爾幹抽調的援兵。俄羅斯帝國是這場戰爭的第三方：1806年已對奧斯曼開戰，1811年在多瑙河攻入巴爾幹。英土開戰逼得奧軍在多瑙河與愛琴海兩面分兵，因此英國在海峽施加的壓力直接決定了東線能推多遠。英方陣營還包括英國在半島與地中海的盟友葡萄牙與西班牙，但他們並未投入海峽方向的主力，作戰序列自始至終以皇家海軍為核心，戰役的勝負也在海軍與奧軍野戰兵之間判定，而非在倫敦與君士坦丁堡的文書之間。
countriesEn: One side of the conflict was the Royal Navy of the British Empire. Its command had two layers: the Admiralty in London set policy and shifted squadrons, while the highest authority in the Mediterranean was an admiral-in-chief, and the force that actually opened fire in the straits was the squadron of Sir John Thomas Duckworth, built around seventy-four-gun ships of the line, with frigates and a detachment of Royal Marines for boarding work. The British aim was to obtain free passage through the Dardanelles and simultaneously to weaken France's partner in the eastern Mediterranean; from 1806, when the Franco-Ottoman alliance was concluded, this requirement became urgent. The other side was the Ottoman Empire. Its navy answered to the Kapudan Pasha, with its base at Constantinople and among the Aegean islands; its army answered to the Grand Vizier and the serasker, drawing on the ocak regular infantry, the provincial armies of Anatolia and Rumelia, the sipahi cavalry, and detachments sent from the Crimea, the Caucasus and the Balkans. The Russian Empire was the third party to this war. Russia had been at war with the Porte since 1806 and pushed into the Balkans across the Danube in 1811. The Anglo-Turkish war forced the Ottomans to divide between the Danube and the Aegean, so the pressure the British applied in the straits directly decided how far the eastern front could advance. The British camp also included Portugal and Spain, Britain's allies in the peninsula and the Mediterranean, but they committed no main force to the straits; the order of battle remained centred on the Royal Navy from first to last, and the campaign was decided between that navy and the Ottoman field army, not between the paper of London and the paper of Constantinople.
people: 決定戰役走向的是一批海軍將領與朝廷中的角力者。英方最關鍵的人物是約翰·托馬斯·達克沃思爵士，他以五艘戰列艦與三艘巡防艦組成的中隊於1807年5月強行通過達達尼爾海峽，六月十九日在希俄斯灣主動攻擊泊於灣內的奧斯曼分艦隊，一役奠定海上的勝負。英國海軍陸戰隊與皇家炮兵軍官威廉·利克中校隨隊進入海峽，記錄沿岸砲台的數目與配置，成為英方日後論證海峽堡壘弱點的依據。地中海總指揮基思勛爵隨後主持對海峽的長期封鎖，1810年由查爾斯·科頓爵士接任，把封鎖恢復為英國的既定政策。奧方的代表是凱普丹·帕夏，他掌海軍而指揮失當，希俄斯灣之敗後被朝廷問罪；大維齊爾塞義德·馬哈茂德·沙赫一系則在君士坦丁堡主持和戰之爭，蘇丹塞利姆三世在位時力主對英做出讓步，馬哈茂德二世即位後改為拖延求和。陸戰方面，奧軍野戰兵統帥科賈·胡塞因·穆罕默德·帕夏於1811年在魯塞與多瑙河一線連敗；俄軍方面，米哈伊爾·庫圖佐夫元帥率多瑙河方面軍渡河攻擊，彼得·巴爾克海軍上將在黑海牽制奧軍分艦隊。談判桌上，英國外相卡斯特勒雷勛爵主張用奧俄和約帶動英土罷兵，魯米揚采夫代表俄方談判，1812年5月簽訂布加勒斯特條約，英土戰爭隨之收束。
peopleEn: The course of the campaign was decided by a handful of naval commanders and by the factional struggle inside the Ottoman court. The decisive British figure was Sir John Thomas Duckworth, who brought a division of five ships of the line and three frigates through the Dardanelles in May 1807 and, on 19 June, attacked the Ottoman division anchored in the Gulf of Chios, settling the naval question in a single action. Royal Marines and Colonel William Leake of the Royal Artillery went into the straits with him and recorded the number and layout of the shore batteries, which later became the British evidence for the weakness of the Ottoman fortifications. The admiral-in-chief of the Mediterranean, Lord Keith, then directed the long blockade of the straits; in 1810 Sir Charles Cotton took over the command and restored the blockade as settled British policy. The Ottoman representative was the Kapudan Pasha, who commanded the navy but mismanaged the action and was called to account after the defeat in the Gulf of Chios; in Constantinople the Grand Vizier Seyyid Mahmud Shah and his successors ran the debate between war and peace, with Sultan Selim III pressing for concessions to Britain and Mahmud II, once he came to the throne, choosing delay and a search for terms. On land, the Ottoman field army was led by Koca Husrev Mehmed Pasha, who lost in turn at Ruschuk and along the Danube in 1811; on the Russian side General Mikhail Kutuzov led the Danube army across the river in attack, while Admiral Peter Barkov kept the Ottoman division in the Black Sea pinned. At the negotiating table the British Foreign Secretary, Lord Castlereagh, argued for an Ottoman-Russian peace as the lever that would end the Anglo-Turkish war; Rumyantsev spoke for Russia, and the Treaty of Bucharest of May 1812 brought the Anglo-Turkish war to its close.
kits: 任務單上這件長槍出自十六世紀西班牙的大方陣，源頭是「火槍手站在長矛後面」的歐洲火槍與長矛組合。歐洲本國自十七世紀末已廢除步槍長矛，步兵改用火槍加刺刀，但到1807年，長矛仍留在兩處。其一在英國水兵手上：皇家海軍每艘戰列艦都配備約六呎長、帶鐵箍矛頭的登船矛，士兵在甲板防禦與強攻登艦時使用，1807年海峽與希俄斯灣的戰鬥中，登船小組正是靠登船矛與短柄斧壓制甲板上的敵手。其二在奧斯曼陸軍：中央的長矛線仍與火槍配合，密集的矛尖牆排在火槍隊之前。奧軍裝備以燧發滑膛火槍為主，配曲刀、標槍、長柄斧與銅製野戰砲，海峽兩岸則是卡納卡萊與基利特巴希爾兩座堡壘及奇門利克火砲群。英軍裝備是七十四門砲戰列艦的三十二磅主砲與短身砲、火槍刺刀、海軍陸戰隊的刺刀步槍，以及海軍的登船矛；後勤靠馬耳他與錫拉庫薩等地中海基地供應煤、淡水與彈藥，遠距封鎖以軍艦輪替維持。奧軍則以安納托利亞與魯梅利亞行省徵糧，銅料與火藥多仰賴歐洲進口，封鎖一旦持久，內地供應的緊張就會直接反映到海峽守軍的火力上。
kitsEn: The pike named in the task sheet comes out of the sixteenth-century Spanish square, out of the European combination in which the arquebusiers stood behind the pikes. The European powers had abandoned the pike in the pike-and-shot line by the end of the seventeenth century, and infantry had gone over to the musket and bayonet; yet in 1807 the pike survived in two places. The first was in the hands of British sailors: every ship of the line in the Royal Navy carried boarding pikes about six feet long with an iron-shod head, used both to defend the deck and to cut into an enemy ship when boarding, and in the fighting in the straits and in the Gulf of Chios in 1807 it was the boarding pike and the hand axe that cleared the decks of the Ottoman ships. The second was in the Ottoman land army, where the central line of long spears (mizrak) was still combined with the musket, the massed wall of spear points standing in front of the musketeers. The Ottoman equipment list was centred on the flintlock musket (kubur), with scimitars, javelins, long-handled axes and bronze field guns, while the straits were guarded by the fortresses of Canakkale and Kilitbahir and the guns of the Cimenlik battery. The British equipment was the thirty-two-pounder main guns and carronades of the seventy-four-gun ships, the musket and bayonet, the bayonet musket of the Royal Marines, and the boarding pike; the supply system drew coal, fresh water and powder from Mediterranean bases such as Malta and Syracuse, and a distant blockade was kept up by rotating ships in station. The Ottomans drew grain from the Anatolian and Rumelian provinces, relied on Europe for copper and powder, and once the blockade dragged on, the strain of the interior's supply showed directly in the firing power of the garrison in the straits.
tactics: 海戰的關鍵是強行通過海峽。英軍分艦隊以縱隊的戰鬥序列單縷進入海峽，一邊以三十二磅砲壓制兩岸砲台，一邊逐段推進，因海峽最窄處水流湍急，艦隊無法展開，只能縱隊通過；通過後在希俄斯灣主動攻擊奧軍泊地，英軍分成兩翼分進，先以艦砲準備射擊，再以登船編隊強行接舷。封鎖階段，英軍以四至五艘戰列艦在海峽兩端巡弋，攔截出入的奧方商船，令其無法正常裝載貨物。奧軍的戰術完全建立在海峽的地形上：兩岸堡壘與砲台構成交叉火網，分艦隊泊在希俄斯灣內，倚賴岸砲掩護，不願在開放水面作遠洋決戰，一旦被逼出海灣，岸砲的支援立刻消失。陸戰方面，1811年俄軍在多瑙河架設浮橋渡河，以縱隊與縱深射擊交替掩護向前推進；奧軍在魯塞與斯洛博齊亞方向以掘壕、柴柵和密集的火槍長矛線抵抗，試圖用防禦陣地耗盡俄軍攻勢，最終在斯洛博齊亞一役陣線崩潰，野戰兵退守舒門。整場戰爭的戰術邏輯很單純：英國用海峽的幾何限制換取岸砲的沉默，再以封鎖製造奧斯曼的經濟與兵員壓力，迫使其在多瑙河前線分兵。
tacticsEn: The naval problem was how to force the straits. Duckworth's division went through in line ahead, the narrow channel and its fast current giving the ships no room to deploy: the squadron entered in single line, using the thirty-two-pounders to work along the shore batteries and silence them section by section. Having passed, the British attacked the Ottoman anchorage in the Gulf of Chios in two wings, preparing the position with gunfire from the line and then bringing the boarding parties alongside. During the blockade, four to five ships of the line patrolled the two ends of the straits, stopping Ottoman merchantmen and preventing them from loading their cargoes. The Ottoman tactical scheme was built entirely on the geography of the straits: the fortresses and shore batteries laid down a crossfire, and the division lay at anchor inside the Gulf of Chios, relying on the protection of the shore guns and refusing to fight a general action in open water. Once driven out of the gulf, the ships immediately lost that support. On land, in 1811 the Russians bridged the Danube and advanced with alternating columns and covering fire. The Ottomans at Ruschuk and towards Slobozia answered with entrenchments, felled timber and dense lines of musket and pike, hoping to exhaust the Russian attack behind fixed works; the line finally broke at Slobozia and the field army fell back towards Shumen. The logic of the whole campaign is simple: Britain used the geometry of the straits to silence the shore guns, and then used the blockade to squeeze the Ottoman economy and recruitment until the Porte had to split its forces in front of the Danube.
data: 達達尼爾海峽全長約六十一公里，最窄處不足三公里，兩端的堡壘加上沿岸數十門火砲構成咽喉的火力。1807年5月強行通過的分艦隊由五艘戰列艦（勝利號、雷霆號、卡諾普斯號、阿賈克斯號、斯賓塞號）與三艘巡防艦組成，另有數艘小型單桅帆船；希俄斯灣一役，英軍以這支小隊面對集結在灣內的奧軍約十九艘大小帆船，其中數艘為戰列艦，結果奧軍五艘戰列艦被焚、三艘被俘，英軍自身損失有限但並非毫髮無傷。封鎖時期英軍維持四至五艘戰列艦在海峽巡弋，1807年底啟動、延續至1809年，1810年再度恢復。陸戰的數字在各家記載中出入頗大：1811年多瑙河方面俄軍投入數萬兵力，奧軍在魯塞與斯洛博齊亞的野戰兵同樣以數萬計，多瑙河渡口與舒門一線的堡壘、糧秣數目缺乏一致記載，此處不列確數。可以用確證的，是幾個日期與條約：1809年1月5日簽訂《達達尼爾條約》，英奧以此確認通航安排；1812年5月16日《布加勒斯特條約》簽訂，奧斯曼割讓比薩拉比亞予俄國，俄土戰爭與英土戰爭同年收束。
dataEn: The Dardanelles run about sixty-one kilometres end to end, less than three kilometres at their narrowest, and the fortresses at each end, with several dozen shore guns between them, made the throat of the straits. The division that forced its way through in May 1807 was made up of five ships of the line — Victory, Thunderer, Canopus, Ajax and Spencer — together with three frigates and several small single-masted vessels. In the Gulf of Chios this small force confronted an Ottoman concentration of about nineteen sail of every rating, several of them ships of the line; five Ottoman ships of the line were burned and three captured, while the British losses were light but by no means nil. Throughout the blockade the British kept four to five ships of the line patrolling the straits, a blockade begun at the end of 1807 and maintained through 1809, then resumed in 1810. The land figures differ from one authority to the next: in 1811 the Russians committed tens of thousands on the Danube, and the Ottoman field army at Ruschuk and Slobozia was likewise counted in tens of thousands, while the number of the fortresses, the ferries and the stores on the Shumen line is not consistently recorded, and no precise figure is given here. What can be stated with certainty is a set of dates and treaties: the Treaty of the Dardanelles was signed on 5 January 1809, confirming the passage arrangements between Britain and the Porte, and the Treaty of Bucharest was signed on 16 May 1812, the Porte ceding Bessarabia to Russia, which ended the Russo-Turkish war and, in the same year, the Anglo-Turkish war.
cause: 開戰的直接導火線是1807年5月英軍分艦隊未經奧方同意強行通過達達尼爾海峽，隨即在希俄斯灣攻擊泊地。背後的結構性原因有三層。第一層是俄土戰爭：1806年奧斯曼驅逐俄國駐君士坦丁堡的大使，兩國開戰，英國在君士坦丁堡的既有商約隨之受影響。第二層是法國：拿破崙在1806年與奧斯曼締結同盟，奧軍的戰艦與港口一旦為法國所用，英國通往印度的航路與東地中海的商業利益就會直接受威脅，英國亟需在歐洲戰事之外拉開一條牽制線。第三層是海峽的商業權益：英國要求在奧斯曼水域內自由通航、保障英籍商船不受攔截，而奧方在戰事吃緊時收緊了查驗，英國商船屢遭扣留，兩國外交關係因此急轉直下。直接觸發的則是一份英方的通航要求被拒，隨即以艦隊開道的做法代替外交交涉。值得注意的是，決定開戰與否的並非英國議會或奧斯曼的宗教動機，而是同一條水道上的航權、封鎖與反封鎖。
causeEn: The immediate trigger was the British squadron's passage through the Dardanelles in May 1807 without Ottoman consent, followed by the attack on the anchorage in the Gulf of Chios. Behind it lay three structural causes. The first was the Russo-Turkish war: in 1806 the Porte expelled the Russian ambassador at Constantinople and the two empires went to war, which disturbed the commercial arrangements Britain held in the Ottoman capital. The second was France: Napoleon's alliance with the Ottoman Empire in 1806 meant that Ottoman ships and harbours, once available to France, would directly threaten the British route to India and the commerce of the eastern Mediterranean, so Britain needed a line of pressure outside the European theatre. The third was the commercial value of the straits: Britain demanded free navigation in Ottoman waters and the protection of British merchantmen, while the Porte tightened inspection as the war went on and British ships were repeatedly detained, so the two diplomatic positions closed on each other. What set the war off was an Ottoman refusal of the British demand for passage, answered not with negotiation but with cannon. It is worth noting that neither the British parliament nor Ottoman religious sentiment decided the matter; the cause was the contest over navigation, blockade and counter-blockade on the same waterway.
impact: 戰爭的後果分落在三邊。第一是俄國：1812年5月的《布加勒斯特條約》讓俄國取得比薩拉比亞，多瑙河的下游與普魯特河三角洲的屏障重新排定，1812年6月拿破崙侵入俄境後，英俄之間因奧斯曼而生的裂痕也隨之淡去。第二是英國：海峽的實際控制權與通往印度的航路由皇家海軍掌握，地中海東岸成為英國海權秩序的一部分，1809年《達達尼爾條約》與其後的安排把這種通航特權固定下來。第三是奧斯曼：長達數年的封鎖切斷了外貿與軍火輸入，國庫吃緊，軍隊裝備落後的問題被徹底暴露，塞利姆三世的新軍整頓與馬哈茂德二世的西式改編因此加速，朝廷先後向歐洲派出軍事考察團並聘請外國顧問。戰事也牽動了愛琴海周邊的希臘武裝集團，使其在英奧角力之間獲得活動空間，成為其後希臘人武裝起義的舞台之一。從兵器史的角度看，這五年還標誌著歐洲步兵的長矛時代正式落幕：長矛退守到海軍的登船矛與奧軍的中央矛線，歐洲本土的方陣長矛再也沒有回到戰場。
impactEn: The consequences of the war fell on three parties. The first was Russia: the Treaty of Bucharest of May 1812 gave her Bessarabia and reordered the screen on the lower Danube and the Pruth delta, and after Napoleon's invasion of Russia in June 1812 the Anglo-Russian estrangement born of the Ottoman question faded. The second was Britain: real control of the straits and of the route to India passed to the Royal Navy, the eastern Mediterranean became part of the British maritime order, and the Treaty of the Dardanelles of 1809 and the arrangements that followed locked in that privilege of passage. The third was the Ottoman Empire: a blockade lasting years cut off foreign trade and the import of arms, the treasury came under strain, and the backwardness of the army was laid bare. Selim III's reform of the new army and Mahmud II's westernising overhaul were thereby hastened, the court sending military missions to Europe and hiring foreign advisers. The fighting also stirred the Greek armed bands of the Aegean, who found room to operate between Britain and the Porte, one of the stages for the Greek risings that came later. From the history of arms the five years also mark the formal end of the European pike era: the pike retreated to the boarding pike of the navy and to the central spear line of the Ottoman army, and never returned to the European battlefield.

resultEn: The outcome was a complete British success at sea and a Russian success on land, with the Ottomans caught between the two. In the Gulf of Chios in June 1807 the Ottoman division was practically destroyed, five ships of the line burned and three captured, and the Kapudan Pasha was dismissed; the shore batteries of the straits lay under permanent British command of the water, Ottoman merchant traffic was restricted, and the division could no longer be concentrated. The land campaign of 1811 went against the Ottomans: Koca Husrev Mehmed Pasha led the field army back step by step at Ruschuk and along the Danube, and the line finally collapsed at Slobozia, with the army falling back on Shumen. Unable to fight on and squeezed by the blockade on supplies and munitions, the Porte signed the Treaty of Bucharest on 16 May 1812, ceding Bessarabia to Russia and making peace with Russia; Britain wound the war up on the arrangements of the Treaty of the Dardanelles of 1809, and the Anglo-Turkish war ended with free passage guaranteed and the blockade of the straits still in force. The war took no Ottoman territory, and its result lay neither in the palace intrigues of Constantinople nor in any territorial annexation, but in two things: Britain took the initiative in the straits, and the Ottoman Empire, pressed by land war and blockade at once, was driven to ask for terms.
